newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: FBI agents investigate Cambodia grenade attack.
newsitem.headline: FBI agents investigate Cambodia grenade attack.

text.p: Three FBI agents, hired by the Cambodian government to look into last month's grenade attack on a Phnom Penh protest rally, on Tuesday visited the site of blast in front of the National Assembly.
The March 30 attack on the rally, led by opposition leader Sam Rainsy, killed nearly 20 people and wounded more than 150, including American Ron Abney of the International Republican Institute.
The agents of the U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation are investigating the worst act of political violence to hit Cambodia since U.N.-sponsored elections in 1993.
The violence worsened relations between co-premier Prince Norodom Ranariddh, an ally of Sam Rainsy, and co-Premier Hun Sen, who formed an uneasy coalition following the 1993 polls.
It also provoked an international outcry, including a letter last week from Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto expressing concern over the grenade attack and growing political tensions.
